evidence.note: Agent loaded a task-tracking tool then created 9 explicit, ordered milestones: skeleton+/_health, DB schema+FTS5+seed, markdown (flagged 'Hardest parity item'), models, Liquid views, routes, header/CSP contracts, job queue with BEGIN IMMEDIATE/retry/backoff, and a parity comparison harness. Each carries an embedded done-signal; risky and foundational pieces are called out — a dependency-aware written plan.

Milestone state tracked via TaskUpdate; markdown milestone marked complete (190-191) only after golden comparisons passed (154, 189), demonstrating a concrete exit check per milestone rather than a vague list.

Job-queue milestone treated as a discrete unit with cross-runtime shared-DB test (447-459) as its exit criterion before being marked completed (465) — evidence of parity checks gating milestone completion across the horizon.

Late milestones (concurrency/latency, interaction parity, admin/audit) continued to be tracked and closed against verification, showing the milestone structure was referenced through the full trajectory, not abandoned early.

reasoning: The agent produced an explicit, dependency-aware subsystem breakdown written into a task system, sequenced sensibly (health/schema before feeds/jobs), flagged risky pieces (markdown, BEGIN IMMEDIATE job queue), and gated each milestone's completion on a concrete parity check referenced throughout — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the plan was authored once and not revised as complexity emerged, and the hardest cross-runtime shared-state interface (job claim semantics) was sequenced late rather than de-risked first.
